source_review.notes: Checked all six references for identity, date, and cited scope. Bell et al. ICSE 2018 supports rerun limitations and differential-coverage flake detection. Lam et al. ICST 2019 supports order-dependent and non-order-dependent classification by reordered and repeated execution. Current Google Testing Blog guidance supports causes across tests, frameworks, systems and dependencies, operating systems, hardware, and networks, plus condition waits instead of arbitrary delays. Current pytest documentation supports flakiness risks under parallel execution and order/state diagnostics. Zhang et al. ISSTA 2014 supports ordered-environment test dependence and its consequences. Verified Meszaros bibliographic metadata. Checked 2026-09-06.

evidence: Defined binary outcome variables, constant failure probability, independent executions, detection target, logarithmic run bound, and execution-record tuple before use.
Checked probability, complement, exponent, logarithm, inequality, domain assumptions, set notation, tuple notation, and all GitHub math delimiters.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The independent constant-probability model is explicitly bounded and not presented as a universal CI model.

evidence: Executed flaky-ci-model under CPython 3.14.4 and matched seven exact outputs with empty stderr and exit status zero.
Recomputed 0.9^10 = 0.3486784401, complement 0.6513215599, and rounded outputs 0.3487 and 0.6513.
Checked detection threshold: 1-0.9^28 is below 0.95 while 1-0.9^29 is above 0.95.
Recomputed exercise values 0.95^20 approximately 0.3585 and complement approximately 0.6415.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Probabilities are model calculations, not measured production rates.

evidence: Derived all-pass probability as the product (1-p)^n under independence and at-least-one-failure as its complement.
Solved 1-(1-p)^n >= q by logarithms and checked that division by negative log(1-p) reverses the intermediate inequality to produce the stated lower bound.
Checked domain restrictions 0<p<1 and 0<q<1.
Checked execution identity tuple separates subject, test, attempt, order, seed, and environment.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: No independence or stationarity is inferred from observed CI attempts.

evidence: Reviewed zero and rare failure probability, finite passing samples, correlated runs, changing probability, fixed and varied seeds, isolated and ordered runs, serial and parallel execution, and heisenbug effects.

Reviewed leaked fixtures, shared accounts, files, ports, databases and registries, wall and monotonic clocks, sleeps, bounded condition waits, timeouts at multiple layers, public networks, mutable services, rate limits, and runner loss.

Reviewed product races, test defects, environment defects, infrastructure loss, fail-pass and pass-fail transitions, retry erasure, permanent quarantine, non-quarantinable claims, deleted assertions, sensitive diagnostics, and metric gaming.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Diagnosis must preserve uncertainty because categories can overlap.

evidence: Traced exact subject, artifact, test, data, configuration, dependencies, runner, platform, resources, clock, seed, order, shard, attempt, network, and time through each outcome.
Checked initial failure and all reruns remain separate and final-pass selection is prohibited.
Checked test, product, environment, and infrastructure classifications retain distinct gate and repair semantics.
Checked quarantine retains execution, inventory, lost-claim visibility, owner, issue, expiry, controls, and exit criteria.
invariant_checking.notes: Quarantine restores blocking-suite signal only by explicitly accepting missing trustworthy evidence.

evidence: Reviewed the probability derivation and negative-log inequality direction.
Reviewed contradictory-evidence preservation and confirmed selecting only the last attempt is not faithful aggregation.
Reviewed the A then B versus B then A state-leak counterexample and isolated-rerun limitation.
Reviewed quarantine invariant and confirmed an unreliable result cannot continue satisfying its former blocking claim.
proof_review.notes: The arguments establish properties of stated models and records, not universal test determinism.

evidence: Audited uses of flaky, same, independent, probability, proof, reproduce, pass, fail, stable, deterministic, reliable, fixed, and verified.
Confirmed mathematical assumptions, empirical paper findings, current guidance, hypothetical scenarios, professional policy, and local execution are separated.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The chapter explicitly rejects finite passing samples as a stability certificate.

evidence: Executed the sole practical snippet under CPython 3.14.4 with declared exact stdout, empty stderr, and exit status zero.
Confirmed model probabilities, run threshold, order-dependent behavior, sleep and retry limitations, and quarantine inventory count.
Confirmed all CI, UI, payment, infrastructure, seed, account, quarantine, and repair examples are hypothetical teaching situations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No real test suite, CI job, external service, runner fleet, flake detector, or production quarantine was executed or measured.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed the complete chain from defining intended sameness through outcome preservation, cause classification, replay capture, order, time, randomness, external state, designed reruns, probabilistic limits, quarantine, root-cause repair, measurement, and seeded control testing. Flaky tests, flaky jobs, product defects, and infrastructure loss remain distinct.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed failures across retry erasure, wrong-subject reruns, missing seeds and orders, fixture leaks, parallel races, sleeps, clock misuse, shared services, rate limits, mutable dependencies, runner loss, ambiguous timeouts, hidden assertions, quarantine debt, critical lost coverage, sensitive logs, and misleading final-status metrics. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified undergraduate progression from precise vocabulary and an order leak through detection probability derivation, four bounded arguments, one executable seven-outcome model, eight trade-off pairs, eighteen misconceptions, ten distinct situations, and five exercises progressing from distinctions through calculation, diagnosis, quarantine design, and measurement audit.

limitations: Internal authoring, source, mathematical, executable-model, conceptual, practitioner, and pedagogical evidence only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Papers and current guidance, independent-run probability calculations, deterministic state examples, hypothetical cases, and one local model execution do not establish any production flake rate, test independence, root cause, quarantine safety, test adequacy, CI reliability, or repair effectiveness.
